messages:
oliver_ap: FYI vendor CloudTools Inc (US) sent invoice with a state sales tax line. They asked us to provide a resale/exemption cert or else to gross-up so they get the tax back. Can tax confirm policy?

maria_taxes: Tagging @taxbot. Quick: we don't gross-up for sales tax. If the sale is taxable in the vendor's state they must collect unless we provide a valid exemption certificate for that state. Need copy of cert and confirmation that purchase is for resale or exempt purpose.

jo_procurement: Pasted invoice excerpt: ```
Invoice: CT-2026-881
Vendor: CloudTools Inc
Amount: USD 4,500
State sales tax (CA 7.25%): USD 326.25
Total: USD 4,826.25
Note: "Please provide resale certificate or we will collect tax"
```

sam_sales: This is for a customer demo environment hosted in Oregon but billed to Redwood HQ (registered in CA). We normally apply our CA resale certificate for product purchases. Do we have a CA resale cert on file?

maria_taxes: We only have a CA resale cert on file for one of our product purchasing entities, not for HQ billing entity. Need to know which legal entity is being billed and whether the purchase is for resale/transfer to customers. If it's a service consumed by Redwood (not resale), CA tax likely applies.

taxbot: Internal note: resale certificates are state-specific (e.g., CA CDTFA resale certificate) and must be issued to the vendor's name and include our seller's permit/TIN. We can provide the cert only if the transaction qualifies as resale or exempt by statute. See internal link: https://tax-docs.internal/us-sales-tax (internal).

oliver_ap: Reached out to vendor asking them to hold payment and to confirm the billed legal entity. Also asked procurement to confirm purpose (resale vs internal use).

jo_procurement: Confirmed with sales: this is for internal SaaS integration for demos (not sold to customers). So it is not resale.

sam_sales: Ok noted. We routed the billing to Redwood CA entity because of card limits. That means CA sales tax could be due. Is there an automatic way to avoid vendor collecting tax?

maria_taxes: If it's not resale, we cannot issue a resale cert. Options: 1) pay invoice including tax (no gross-up by Redwood) or 2) ask vendor to remove sales tax if they accept that the transaction is non-taxable (but unlikely), or 3) change billing to an entity or jurisdiction where supplier has no nexus and won't collect. But we must be careful about substance. Also consider reimbursement treatment.

taxbot: Practical: do not agree to gross-up requests. Gross-up sets precedent and would shift tax burden to Redwood. If vendor insists they need net, suggest alternative commercial solutions (faster payment, partial prepay) but not tax gross-up.

oliver_ap: I proposed to vendor: we can (A) provide a valid resale/exemption cert if purchase qualifies, or (B) remit full invoice including sales tax, or (C) change billing entity if operationally possible. Asked them which they prefer.

vendor_replies (copied): "We prefer resale cert or we'll collect tax. If you can't provide, please remit full amount. Gross-up not accepted by our accounting either."

jo_procurement: If vendor won't accept entity change, we'll approve paying tax for this one-off but log guidance: require billing to our expense entity that has certificate for future purchases.

maria_taxes: Final: AP will not gross-up. If we determine the transaction is taxable and no resale cert applies, pay the invoice including tax. Procurement to adjust billing or contract terms for future to avoid CA sourcing when not necessary. Note: retain invoice + correspondence for audit.

oliver_ap: Marked AP hold released and processed payment including tax after confirmation from procurement. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
